heuristics.extrapolation: Historical 15-column scans and the inherited 11-column panels support the uniformity premise. Current 13-column semantic controls, the complete census and the base's 14-column controls are in Appendix U. Finite parity does not prove H1 or deep acceptance.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about the 38-step first-block compression; the experiments use deterministic seed expansion and reduced sizes; full-scale runs cover seven chaining values.
heuristics.scope: Expected per_a0=11.90333637932078201878...; claws/a0=160*E/2^32, C1-claws/a0=20*E/2^32, E in [32,581,626, 32,676,574]. H1 supports the postfilter law, Bernstein cap and independence across fresh first blocks. The proven walk mean bound 7 follows equal per-entry C1 mass and prefix retention; the ledger charges 6.770000 under H1W and step 3b at its mean 842.361097 under H3B; the maximum is 18/read. The three omitted relative columns (12, 13 and 14) are fixed before outcomes.
heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings and their chaining values cv = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: (a) for every a0, F(a0) = Cc2 + a0 + k0 + h(a0) is uniform and independent of h(a0) and of the epoch's table (cv[7] enters k0 additively and nothing else; cv[6] enters h(a0) additively), and cv[0] is uniform given both; hence y = R16H[0] - r - F(a0) is uniform, a window probes with probability 186/8192, a probe makes 2860/93 reads, the expected claw count of an a0 is 160 E / 2^32 for the table's E retained entries (Lemma C), and a claw's a1 = u - h(a0) is uniform and independent of the claw event, so a claw passes C1 with probability 1/8 (proof.md Sections 3.6, 5, 6); (b) given the epoch's table, the works W_j and the success counts X_j of distinct chaining values are independent (Lemma 3, Section 7). For each retained entry separately, H1 gives 160/2^32 expected claws and 20/2^32 expected C1 claws per scanned a0. Every bucket holds a prefix of at most six lanes; weights 6,6,6,8,8,8 sum to at most 7p for population p. Thus the ordered-tree mean charge is at most 7 per C1 claw for every fixed table, without independence between lanes or conditioning cost on success.

heuristics.extrapolation: Four complete 11-column tables, 500,000 H1-uniform probes each (r=8174 and r=4401, the two extremes of E, at ustart=0; r=8174 at ustart=0x9e3779b9; r=663 at ustart=0xff5baf92): ratio means 6.739121, 6.737195, 6.750949, 6.738023 (se about 0.0040), 0 lane mismatches; the charge 6.770000 lies above the largest 99% upper bound, 6.760092. Each table mean averages 5,767,168 buckets of one population law.
heuristics.limitations: Measured on four of the 2^13 x 2^32 epoch tables by Monte Carlo probes; the full-table runs omit the 5 frame-crossing reads of 156 per probe. Under H1 alone the proven bound 7 gives time_log2 76.51858.
heuristics.scope: The per C1-claw cost 24.405795... and per_a0 11.903336... (proof Section 5, Appendix A), hence wbar and Lemma 3's E[W_j | tables] <= wbar. Not used for vmax, the Lemma 2 cap or the success probability.
heuristics.statement: For every epoch table (every r in [0, 2^13) and every ustart), the mean charge of the ordered lane walk walk_lanes per C1 claw, over the H1-uniform probe position (column, row, w) and PHI, is at most 6.770000 operations. The ledger charges this mean (WALK_MEAN) in place of the proven bound 7 of H1; the exact maximum 18 per nonempty read is unchanged and stays in vmax.

heuristics.extrapolation: Two complete 11-column tables (E_HI, E_LO), 8 class-kept chaining values each: 1,225 good pairs, pooled ratio 841.992653 (se 0.089315), 0 reference mismatches; the per-table normal 99% bounds (842.361097 at r=8174 is charged) are nominal supporting estimates (proof Appendix U.3).
heuristics.limitations: Declared model: the calls share 16 chaining values, and two tables do not cover every table; single-CV tallies may exceed the charge (r=4401, s3b|4: 842.549), which the per-table expectation allows.
heuristics.scope: The step-3b term of the per C1-claw cost (8 q_pf_hi x 842.361097 = 0.372524...), hence per_a0 11.903336..., wbar and Lemma 3's E[W_j | tables] <= wbar. Not used for vmax, OVER, the Lemma 2 cap or the success probability.
heuristics.statement: For each fixed epoch table T, with a fresh class-kept chaining value CV drawn under H1, let G_T(CV) be the number of step3b calls (step3b stops at its first failing row test) and S_T(CV) their total counted work; then E[S_T(CV) | T] <= 842.361097 E[G_T(CV) | T]. The ledger charges this ratio (STEP3B_MEAN) in place of the longest path 3,014, which stays in vmax and OVER. No bound for each CV and no independence of call count and cost is assumed.

heuristics.extrapolation: The inherited exhaustive N12/G counts and real-word controls remain in Sections 3.7/6 and the historical archive. All 5,422 isolated native-pair checks agree with the retained predicates. The restriction retains the stated H1/H7 transfer premises.
heuristics.limitations: F7's per-chaining-value spread makes few-chaining-value measurements of the good-pair rate noisy; the expectation over a uniform chaining value is what the bound uses.
heuristics.scope: q_pf(SEL) in N_CV and the post-filter chain term of the per-C1-claw cost (24.405795 operations per C1-claw with the class, walk and step-3b mean included).
heuristics.statement: For the claws the u-table procedure finds, Pr[C1 and C2 and G and F7] = q_pf = 57,726,359,870,197 x 287,309,824 / 2^90 = 2^-16.1877, the rate enumerated exhaustively over all 2^32 words (P(C1) = 1/8, |C1 and C2| = 53,096,854, the W9 G count 57,726,359,870,197, |F7| = 287,309,824); the stage rates 1/8, 2^-6.3379, 2^-12.2857 set the mean post-filter cost. In this filing C1 is decided inside the bucket test (Lemma B''), so the procedure processes the C1-claws (one eighth of the claws) and the rates P(C2 | C1) = 8 x 53,096,854 / 2^32 and P(C2 G | C1) set the remaining chain cost; the good-pair set is unchanged (Lemma C1). With the window (Section 3.7) the G rate is the exact count over SEL, P(G | C1 C2, SEL) = 2,051,404,269,120 / (2^20 x 53,096,854) = 0.0368453386, and F7 stays at |F7|/2^32: q_pf(SEL) = 2^-15.0022. With the kept class of chaining values (H9) F7 is at the class's rate: q_pf(SEL, class) = 2^-14.1609 at F7R = 0.11985.

heuristics.extrapolation: Registered P1/base q3 and paired runs, diagnostics and lower bounds remain in Section 9 and historical P/Q. No new rare-event measurement is substituted. The independent current-minimum calculation confirms K*p_max<2^-28.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run sequential Monte Carlo with a heavy-tailed middle stage; the deep rows (about 2^-71 per good pair) are not measurable directly; premises (a) and (b) are not measured on the P1 family (sensitivity of (a): up to about 0.37 bit of time_log2 if the gain were absent); the u-table's retention weighting of u is covered by H7.
heuristics.scope: q3r, hence N_CV and the whole attack term; the upper form (c) only bounds the second-order factor (1 - 2^-25) of the epoch argument (proof.md Section 7, Lemma T).
heuristics.statement: A good pair of the u-table procedure is accepted by step 3b with probability q3r >= q3_P1 x 2^32 / 160 = 2^-71.4010, where q3_P1 = 2^-96.0791 = q3_model x 2^D_LB: q3_model = 2^-96.0133 is the registered accepted-event rate of the A0-variant good pairs on P8 before row 16 and D_LB = -0.0658 is the registered one-sided 99% lower bound of the paired per-seed difference L(P1) - L(A0) measured with the P1 law of the window W9 = [9 x 2^26, 10 x 2^26) (a0 uniform in W9 given G, a1 uniform on C1 and C2). Every a0 the procedure scans lies in W9 (the restriction to the sub-blocks SEL of W9 is the separate premise H8), its claws' a1 are uniform (H1) and its good pairs have the measured (a0, a1) law; their u = W1 is a retained table word, uniformly thinned by the epoch's rotation r (Lemma S) and retained by the arc law (H7). Two inherited transfer premises are part of this heuristic and are stated in proof.md Section 9: (a) the relaxation gain (+0.41488 bit for not imposing E18 = E17), measured on the A0-variant family, is the same for the P1 family, whose paired difference D_LB was measured on the printed event; (b) q3 does not depend on the re-weighting of a1 by its G count n(a1), the difference between the R9 list law (a1 uniform on C1 and C2, then a0 given G) and the u-table's joint law. (c) For the second-order term of the epoch argument only, the average acceptance a-bar of good pairs with uniform W1 is at most 2^10 q3r = 2^-61.40 (the one-sided 99% upper readings of the same registered runs give 2^-70.88). Lemma T then bounds the acceptance of every table's good pairs by 2^6.8013 a-bar, because each table holds at least 38,510,323 of the 2^32 words and acceptance is nonnegative.

heuristics.extrapolation: The inherited registered estimator, confidence interpretation and limitations remain in Section 9 and historical P/Q/R. No finite current check validates a probability near 2^-96.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run tool, not executed by the organizer; heavy-tailed middle stage (some ratio seeds die, counted as 0); the estimator is validated on known answers and on its own reproductions, not on an independent implementation.
heuristics.scope: q3_model and D_LB, hence q3r, N_CV and the attack term (the same scope as H2-P1).
heuristics.statement: The sequential Monte Carlo estimator traillab (the lineage's own C tool, not shipped), with which q3_model and the paired difference D_LB were measured, estimates the accepted-event rate of the stated model without material bias. It replays every sample on real 38-step compressions of both members (0 replay mismatches required), treats rows 16..21 as the importance-split prefix (8,192 particles, 256 proposals per row; the row-16 stage is exact with weight 160/2^32) and counts EXACT (zero output difference after step 37) in the window rows 22..37. Its per-seed values, combined by the registered one-sided rules, give conservative bounds for the true rate.

heuristics.extrapolation: The registered 24-CV panel retains its DEPENDENCE DETECTED result, unequal-size caveat and post-hoc rate comparison in Section 8 and historical H. The restriction does not strengthen this premise.
heuristics.limitations: Not testable at the acceptance probability; components only. The 24-CV panel was not stratified by the cv0 class, and the marginal class-rate measurements (F7R, MSG_CLS on an independent pool) do not by themselves establish a factorial-moment inequality, so the class-conditioned transfer is declared, not measured.
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor (1 - 2^-8.5) per chaining value in the success bound and the epoch second-order term, for uniform and for class-kept chaining values.
heuristics.statement: Group independence within a chaining value (the form of H5-group-independence of the accepted 44870635): good pairs of one chaining value that share no endpoint (a0 or u) are independent trials of the accepted event, each with probability q3r; good pairs sharing an endpoint form a group counted once. Consequence used: for a uniform chaining value and any table, J (accepted good pairs among all claws of the chaining value) has E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]. This filing applies the same premise to the kept-CV class ((cv0 >> 24) & 63 == 12): the class conditions only cv[0], the panel below is drawn from uniform chaining values (so about 1/64 of its CVs are in-class), and the transfer of the second-moment bound to the class-conditioned law is part of this declared premise.

heuristics.extrapolation: Section 4 and Appendix U list prices. Exact register/walk controls, the isolated actual ledger, independent rational reconstruction, 18 restriction/ledger source mutants and six isolated method mutants bind changed terms. Observations are participant evidence.
heuristics.limitations: Prices are the cost model's unit prices applied to an explicit straight-line count; the 256-bit word tests rely on the absence of carries between lanes and between the u part and the field of a lane, proved in Lemmas B' and B'' and checked on every lane class.
heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, C=2728. Each load/store/address/arithmetic/logic/shift/immediate/random operation costs 1; compare plus branch costs 2; a branch on a zero test of a computed word costs 1 (Lemma Z: the read's Z = 0 test and three single-bit pf_tail tests); sigma costs 8 (post-filter s0 tests 6, Lemma D); folded MAJ/CH costs 2. Section 4 prices the build, the 16 random words of M0 per first block, class test, per-CV setup, 218-operation 16-register program, probe rate 186/8192, 2860/93 reads per probe, seven-operation read, walk mean 6.770000/C1 claw (H1W) and maximum 18/read, postfilter segments 13, 22 and 24, step3b mean 842.361097/good pair (H3B) and maximum 3014 in vmax, and one-time 2^24 initialization. No cost is inferred from wall time.

heuristics.extrapolation: Eleven fresh fixed-seed controls with a local source build of Kissat 4.0.1: three satisfiable with rows decoded, two unsatisfiable and six undecided under a conflict budget, so only three exercise row decoding. In all eleven the solver read exactly the published serializer's bytes (tapped). 24 file-against-pipe solver configurations, five local PySAT builds and exact LP-dual certificates checked by two programs. The live clause objects at the end of construction were measured on seven sweep-shaped controls, each bound to its control's formula. No historical P8 run is re-executed.
heuristics.limitations: H6-D is not reproduced locally: on the experiment platform the published encoder at the end of construction exceeds 152,868 KiB (no blocks: 158,711,808 bytes anonymous, 168,951,808 resident; 5,430 blocks: 166,572,032 and 176,832,512). Under Appendix Z the record costs at most half the tail, so phase E rises 1.5 bytes per byte of encoder-figure understatement; the cell (184,725,504) is 6,115,360 below the analytical image and 8,765,440 below the charge. The historical Kissat 4.0.1 binary and platform are unavailable; parity uses a local source build. Fresh fixed-seed controls, not a historical reproduction. Live clause objects: receipt results/clause-objects.json, SHA-256 9cfaaa6ea889d583..., Appendix W section 6. The record bound uses the encoder figure only for the live clause objects; on the experiment platform these occupy at most about 128.6 MB allocator-rounded, about 28 MB below 152,868 KiB, while the whole process is 169–177 MB resident.
heuristics.scope: Appendix W: the record bound 44,585,056 bytes, needing no Kissat premise, and the P8 cell 211,431,424, whose phases R and S use H6-D figure and the H6-E(b) allowances. Appendix Z brings the cell to 184,725,504, above the image 175,112,224 and below the predecessor's charge; time, preprocessing and success are unchanged.
heuristics.statement: (a0) The 152,868 KiB encoder figure of H6-D bounds the live clause objects of the historical P8 encoder process at the end of construction (every clause list of F_hist with its item array, and the int objects outside -5..256 held by its sha256_model clauses), resident and not swapped out or compressed; these are the only objects the record and token bounds read, and R.6D does not use this reading. (a) The encoder ran on a default 64-bit CPython 3: each clause of F_hist was a distinct list of at least 56+8k bytes, each literal sdmodel.apply computed outside the small-int cache -5..256 a distinct int object of at least 26 bytes, and PySAT's CNF kept each clause as that list or a copy holding the same objects. (b) The measured P8RR allowances transfer to the historical platform: recorder overhead 2 MiB, regenerator 32 MiB, decoder 96 MiB, filter 1 MiB, launcher 4 MiB, 1 MiB kernel state per process, 1 MiB for Kissat reading a pipe, 1 MiB per pipe; retained files are rounded to 4 KiB pages. (d) Assumed: the spec was shorter than 2 MiB, as one execve argument of the published sweep allows on Linux with pages of at most 64 KiB or on macOS; it bounds the launcher's, decoder's and output's copies of the spec.

heuristics.extrapolation: The exact eleven-column census reconstructs all 8,192 totals and satisfies 15*291542711184=12*364428388980, with the thirteen-column window 38,510,323..38,610,389 and the 15-column control 44,436,632..44,543,396 as measured cross-checks. Acceptance/retention support remains historical 15-column evidence with unavailable inputs. Appendix T preserves the 38-run sources/records and 65,265,200-byte H7 envelope. Current parity supports implementation only.
heuristics.limitations: Tested only on the shallow rows 17..21 components, not on the deep event (rows 22..37); the retention probability of a covered word ranges with its bucket's population. The historical panel inputs are unavailable; Appendix T does not claim to re-execute them.
heuristics.scope: The success expectation E[X_j] averaged over epoch tables = 2^20 (160 E / 2^32) q_pf(SEL, class) 2^-0.0468 2^-0.0225 q3r of proof.md Section 7. Current extrema are measured census values. H7 remains an explicit averaged acceptance/retention transfer premise for the fixed restriction.
heuristics.statement: Each epoch draws r uniform on [0, 2^13) and ustart uniform on 32 bits; u is covered with probability exactly 96/8192 (Lemma S), and a covered u is retained iff it is among the first six covered words of its bucket. Retained entries E lie in [32,581,626, 32,676,574] for every r (exhaustive over all 8,192 r and all 2^32 words). For fixed r the covered words lie in 96 of the 8,192 classes of P(u) mod 2^13; Lemma S holds averaged over r. Premise: averaged over (r, ustart), acceptance is independent of coverage class and retention, so expected accepted pairs equal expected claws times q_pf times q3r.

heuristics.extrapolation: The exact selected-window counts are in Section 3.7 and Appendix A (N12 = 53,096,854 C1-and-C2 values; G_SEL = 2,051,404,269,120 over the 2^20 selected a0), so the window message factor is an exact post-selection count and the selection statistic (sampled G mass) is message-side. The measurable state events, the rows 17..21 forced-bit panels, are in Appendix T; the inherited message/state argument, registration and per-seed evidence remain in Section 3.7 and Appendix V. Charge 2^-0.0468 is unchanged; parity does not prove rows 22..37 invariance.
heuristics.limitations: Rows 22..37 of the state part are not directly measurable at the claimed probability; H8 is the premise covering exactly that gap, supported by the exact message-side counts, the shallow-row panels and the unchanged registration, not by a measurement of the deep event. If it failed, the bound would move with the state part on the selected good pairs.
heuristics.scope: Inherited historical sensitivity/comparison only: q3r in N_CV and the whole attack term; the window raises q_pf by the exact factor 2.2743 and lowers time_log2 by 1.1122 after the charged message factor.
heuristics.statement: Given the message-difference profile of a good pair (both members' W16..W37), the state part of acceptance (the conditions on the state additions of rows 16..37, and any alternative path) is the same for good pairs with a0 uniform in SEL (4,096 sub-blocks of 256 a0 of W9 with the largest sampled G mass, conditioned on G) as for those with a0 uniform in W9 (the law under which H2-P1 measured q3r). The message part is measured and charged: the window's good pairs are accepted with probability at least 2^-0.0468 q3r = 2^MSG_LO q3r, and their average acceptance satisfies the weak upper form a-bar <= 2^10 q3r used in Lemma T. Selection: SEL was chosen by sampled G mass, but q_pf uses the exact count G_SEL, so the choice does not bias it.

heuristics.extrapolation: The class F7 rate 0.11985 (upper 0.12136) and message factor 2^-0.0225 were measured on pools independent of the class selection, with a second pool for F7R and MSG_CLS, so both factors are post-selection-independent measurements; the class is a 2^-6 cv0 condition with three charged operations per first block. The rows 17..21 panels are in Appendix T; the 64-class search, rates, paired evidence and bounds remain in Section 3.8 and Appendix V. Finite controls do not establish rows 16..37 invariance.
heuristics.limitations: Rows 16..37 of the state part are not directly measurable at the claimed probability; H9 covers that gap, supported by the independent-pool class rates, the balanced 64-class search and the shallow-row panels rather than by a measurement of the deep event. The F7 rate rests on a pool of 2^20 q with 16 sampled cv[0] each.
heuristics.scope: Inherited historical sensitivity/comparison only: q_pf and q3r in N_CV and the step-3b cost term: the class raises q_pf by 0.11985 / 0.0668945 = 2^0.8413 and, after the charged message factor and the class test (3 operations per first block), gives time_log2 76.7653 (without the class: 77.5450; 8116a55c: 77.1297).
heuristics.statement: Only first blocks whose chaining value is in the class ((cv0 >> 24) & 63) == 12 are kept (2^-6 of them; proof.md Section 3.8). (a) Under H1 a kept chaining value has cv[0] uniform in the class and its other words uniform; for the claws of a kept chaining value C1, C2 and G pass at the rates of H1-P1 (they do not read the chaining value), and F7 passes at the class average of the F7 rate over the good-pair law of q, charged at its one-sided 99% lower bound F7R = 0.11985 (the step-3b cost at the upper bound 0.12136). (b) Given the message-difference profile of a good pair (both members' W16..W37), the state part of acceptance is the same for good pairs with cv[0] uniform in the class as for those with cv[0] uniform (the law of H2-P1 and H8). The message part is measured and charged: the class's good pairs are accepted with probability at least 2^-0.0225 x 2^MSG_LO q3r = 2^-0.0693 q3r, and their average acceptance satisfies the weak upper form a-bar <= 2^10 q3r used in Lemma T. The rates used (F7R and MSG_CLS) were measured on a second pool independent of the class selection.

heuristics.statement: SHA-256 commitments in this package preserve the bytes of the historical records they name; they do not authenticate that the named executions occurred with the stated inputs or resources, and several historical seeds, formulas, binaries and platforms are unavailable.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; step 3b accepts a pair only if A34..A37, E34..E37 of both members are equal, so every output is a collision (Lemma 1, proof.md Section 1).

Retain relative columns 0 through 10 before outcomes. NCOL=11, coverage G(u) mod 8192 <88, probe limit 93, 11*2^19 compact 30-byte records plus a 32-byte terminal pad, six ordered 39-bit lanes and first-six cyclic retention. Each lane is u32, a carry gap and six field bits; count is at bit 234. SEL, kept CV class, front end, combined predicate, ordered walk, postfilters and step3b are unchanged. No codec, map or second resident pass is used.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1, H1-P1 with the window's and the class's rates (q_pf = 2^-14.1609: exact G count over SEL, F7 at the class rate 0.11985, H9), H2-P1 (q3r >= 2^-71.4010), H8 (the window's message part charged at 2^-0.0468), H9 (the class's message part charged at 2^-0.0225; state parts unchanged), H3-P1 and H7; Bonferroni per chaining value, independence across first blocks given the table and across epochs, claws at the least retained count over r (proof.md Sections 3.7, 3.8, 6, 7). Current E_LO=32,581,626, E_HI=32,676,574. The conservative minimum ratio is 44,436,632/32,581,626. N_CV is recomputed once from that minimum without another multiplier.
